sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Priya Raman led a review of Kestrel Dispatch's driver mobile app v2 across first run, the stop list, offline completion, accessibility, and notification copy.
The team used a driver starting a 24-stop shift as its working scenario and left the release date and completion control open for later evidence.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Jonas Weber proposed a four-step first-run path that confirms the carrier before asking for location and then shows the first assigned stop.
Mei Tanaka said the stop list can work without background location and that the current app silently logs out the first phone when a driver switches devices.
The stop list will expose the appointment window, address, proof requirement, and status for a 24-stop route without making drivers open every card.
Mei said the amber queued badge failed the team's contrast check, and a screen reader announced the completion control only as 'button.'
Jonas favored swipe-to-complete to reduce accidental taps, while Mei favored an explicit confirmation path for drivers using gloves or assistive technology.
Hannah Cole argued that lock-screen notifications should not expose customer addresses or delivery exceptions.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Priya and Mei agreed that denying background location will not block a driver from viewing assigned stops.
The team agreed that an offline completion remains visibly queued until the server accepts it, and that a route reassignment conflict must preserve the driver's note and show a reason.
The stop list will not silently reorder while a driver scrolls; it will surface dispatch changes for review instead.
Priya deferred the swipe-versus-button choice until both controls can be observed with drivers, including low-signal, glove, large-text, and screen reader use.
Hannah and Mei agreed that queued completions use an in-app message, while lock-screen alerts for route changes or rejections reveal no customer address.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: The team has not chosen between swipe-to-complete and an explicit confirmation button because neither has been tested with drivers in the same scenario.
Mei still needs to specify which server receipt permits the app to say a completion was accepted and how a reassigned stop is rejected.
The team has not validated whether a full day of offline photos and notes can survive a restart, so it did not promise that every attachment works offline.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Priya said a driver with 24 stops needs the next address, required proof, and a real exception at a glance.
Mei warned that calling a locally queued completion 'completed' could cause a driver to call support when dispatch still sees the stop as open.
Hannah said broad offline claims would lead drivers to expect route edits, navigation, and every photo to work without coverage.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Jonas's first prototype moved an offline stop into a completed group with a cloud icon, while dispatch still saw it as open until sync.
Mei said the current app silently logs out the first phone when a driver activates a second device.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Mei objected to swipe-to-complete because gloves, tremor, and screen reader use can make the gesture difficult or undiscoverable.
Jonas objected to a modal after every stop because drivers may complete several stops at one depot or as many as 50 in a day.
Hannah objected to saying 'ready to drive' during first run because the app has not checked the driver's vehicle, documents, or safety.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Jonas will revise first-run screens by Thursday and list, conflict, contrast, and completion-control prototypes by next week.
Mei will document invitation and device-switch failures and define queued, accepted, and rejected receipt states by Friday.
Hannah will revise in-app and lock-screen copy by next week, and Priya will ask Amara to recruit drivers from different route types.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Jonas Weber cannot finalize the conflict wording until Mei Tanaka defines which rejection details the server can identify and expose.
Hannah Cole cannot finalize 'accepted by dispatch' wording until Mei Tanaka confirms what the server receipt guarantees.
Priya Raman will not choose a completion control until the team observes both alternatives with drivers using poor coverage and accessibility settings.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Priya Raman wants a driver on a 24-stop shift to see the next address, proof requirement, and exception without searching through the route.
Mei Tanaka wants offline completions to show whether they are queued, accepted, or rejected rather than implying dispatch has a result it has not received.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Jonas Weber showed a four-step first-run prototype and a compact stop list with address, time window, proof requirement, and status.
Mei Tanaka ran a contrast check and screen reader pass, finding a low-contrast amber queued badge and a completion control announced only as 'button.'
Hannah Cole drafted distinct messages for dispatch route changes, locally queued actions, and server-accepted completions.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: A route reassignment while the driver is offline can cause the server to reject a completion, so the app must preserve the driver's note and show a reason.
Mei Tanaka said the local queue has not been tested with a full day of photos and notes after an app restart.
The current swipe control may be difficult with gloves, tremor, or a screen reader, while a repeated button modal may slow drivers with many stops.
Hannah Cole warned that lock-screen alerts could expose customer addresses or delivery exceptions if they carry stop details.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Background location will not block the stop list, and first run will identify the carrier before asking for permissions.
Offline completion will remain visibly queued until a server result arrives, and route changes will appear for review instead of silently reordering the stop list.
The team deferred swipe versus explicit confirmation until both can be observed with drivers under the same stop scenario.
Accepted completions will not trigger a push by default; route changes and rejected actions may notify the driver without customer detail on the lock screen.

sections.heading: Next steps

Mei Tanaka will document invite and device-switch failures and the queued, accepted, and rejected state contract by Friday.
Hannah Cole will update push and in-app copy by next week, and Priya Raman will ask Amara Nwosu for driver recruits by next week.
